items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: he says, we just hadn't had any drummers kicking no band like that unless it was Chick Webb that just kicked

ctx.x: Yeah, all my uniforms. So I called up Alexander; he said, my goodness, and to be sure that he wanted everything right as it should be, he called whatever tailor he was doing business with and told him he wanted--I think I had fourteen pieces then--one suit for everyone in the band and two for me. So naturally, that one gig and a date or two I had to pay him; well, Chick Webb had just passed and Ella Fitzgerald was his vocalist, and they decided to make Ella Fitzgerald the bandleader, and Alexander had closed out…

decided that we're going to make Ella the band-leader, we're going to have to advertise her as a leader. We just can't say vocalist, so they decided--the corporation owned Ella, owned the Chick Webb band--so they told Alexander and he talked it over and said we'll use Fields some other time, we'll let her run this time and we will put him in right after that, but we have got to build our property.
